newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down 1.41 pct on retail sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down 1.41 pct on retail sales.

text.p: Thai stocks, which moved sluggishly throughout the session due to a lack of fresh incentives to boost investment, closed 1.41 percent lower on Thursday on sales by local retailers, brokers said.
The SET index lost buying sentiment seen over the last five trading days and closed 13.54 points lower to 944.51 on 3.0 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index slipped 1.24 points to 71.33.
"The index fell because of profit taking by local retail investors on several key stocks in the finance and banking sectors," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.

The selling in finance shares continued today as many investors were not pleased with third quarter results of some of the major financial firms announced earlier this week. These firms include Phatra Thanakit and Thailand's largest finance firm, Finance One.

Finance One, which topped the active list on Thursday, falling 3.50 baht to 68.50. It reported a drop in profit in the third quarter to 457.93 million baht from 458.08 million baht the same period in 1995.
Phatra Thanakit's net profit dropped 41.7 percent to 302.50 million baht.
Phatra Thanakit fell 4.50 baht to 89 today.
Large capitalised stocks which declined include Bangkok Bank, which fell two baht to 192, and TelecomAsia, which slipped 0.50 to 49.50.
Brokers said they expected that the index would move in a narrow range on Friday on the absence of positive news.
Support is seen at 933 while resistance is pegged at 963 on Friday, they said.
